steps.text: Combine the raspberries, blueberries, sugar, and water in a small saucepan; bring to a boil and cook at a boil for 5 minutes, scraping the bottom as needed to keep from burning. Reduce heat to low and simmer until thick, about 10 minutes. Serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Blueberry and Raspberry Pancake Topping
raw_recipe.description: This delicious berry sauce for pancakes is made with frozen blueberries and raspberries and comes together in just 20 minutes. It's thick and rich — and good on waffles too!
raw_recipe.name: Blueberry and Raspberry Pancake Topping

recipeInstructions.text: Combine the raspberries, blueberries, sugar, and water in a small saucepan; bring to a boil and cook at a boil for 5 minutes, scraping the bottom as needed to keep from burning. Reduce heat to low and simmer until thick, about 10 minutes. Serve warm.

review.reviewBody: I halved this as it was just my daughter and I, and I used only blueberries since I didn't have any raspberries. I can only imagine how great this is with them! With just blueberries it was lovely. I love how quickly this comes together too. Thanks!
I put it in a pyrex casserole bowl and baked it for 30 min. at 375. I did add 1 Tbs of corn starch also. It thickened while sitting awhile

This was awesome. I used a combination of blackberries and raspberries because that's what I had on hand. I also followed the advise of another reviewer and added 1 T. of lemon juice and 1 T. of cornstarch disolved in 2T. of water. 
The only thing that detracted was all of the seeds. Next time I will run the syrum through a strainer at the end. Definately will be making often!

Super easy to make, but it was a little sweet for me. I strained mine to get rid of the seeds, and used a frozen mixed berry bag. I might cut the sugar down a little next time, but will definitely make again.

I made this topping over vanilla sponge cakes for a dessert. I halved the recipe and threw in a few blackberries to add a little tartness. I used fresh raspberries, blueberries and blackberries. I boiled it for 3 minutes and then simmered on low for 5 minutes. Pour it over the individual sponge cakes and then top with homemade whipped cream. (Wholefoods sells a whipped cream they make, its delicious.) My husband was very impressed. This recipe is very simple and will make any novice in the kitchen look like Emerald! BAM!

I love this sauce! It reminds me of some sauces they serve at IHop. I saw others' reviews and did add 1 tsp of lemon juice and (1 TBs of cornstarch after it reached the boiling point) and I'm sure it made the difference!

Used 6 cups of mixed frozen berries from frozen state (blueberries raspberries, blackberries, and strawberries), 1/2 cup sugar, 3 Tbsp cornstarch (dissolved in 1/4 - 1/2 cup water), 1/4 cup water, 1 Tbsp lemon juice and simmered until thickened. Absolutely delicious.

We love topping our pancakes with fruit syrups and light whipped creme. This is almost perfect-but missing a few simple ingredients. It needs a tsp. of lemon juice and 1 TBSP. cornstarch added to 2 TBSP. water. Add to the rest of the ingredient list, blend then heat the syrup and it will thicken. It will be a syrup more in keeping for pancakes, ice cream topping, etc. Otherwise you have a fruit topping that is absorbed by your pancakes rather than laying on top of them. If you don't like seeds, mash, then strain the seeds, (that's a lot of work though...) Easy, Tasty, winner recipe. Thanks!

I made this sauce to use as a cheesecake topping and it was delicious! After a quick taste in the final few minutes of cooking, I did follow other reviewers' suggestions and added 1 Tbsp lemon juice as well as 1 Tbsp cornstarch. Fabulous recipe! Will definitely make this again!

Very good topping. I rated this a 4 stars based on original recipe; but, it's actually 5 stars with my adjustments. I used all fresh raspberries and blueberries, not frozen. I also squeezed fresh orange juice in place of the water. In addition to that I added the zest of the whole orange for more of an orange-y flavor. I found I had to add a little cornstarch to thickened up the sauce as it was too thin. The sauce is BERRYlicious - just sweet enough with a little "tart". The addition of the orange juice and zest gives this sauce a wonderful flavor. I am glad I thickened this up with cornstarch because it has the consistency I wanted. I also plan on using it over pancakes and for another dessert!

I made this using 2 1/2 c. blueberries, 1 T cornstarch and 1 T lemon juice. I put the blueberries, sugar and cornstarch in a pan, mixed that, then added the water and lemon juice. I then followed the rest of the recipe instructions. The flavor was excellent. However, it was a bit thinner than I liked. I will try adding more cornstarch next time. This is definitely a keeper recipe!
My family loved it so much that we made it like five times,so I hope you post more dealishes foods.

I’ve made this with blueberries, the blueberry and raspberry mix, and black cherries. It’s delicious. I plan on trying out every berry! I did like others suggested and I add 1 tablespoon of lemon juice and I actually add 2 tablespoons of corn starch. It’s lovely.
Everyone in our family loved it. I followed the recipe exactly, and it thickened perfectly. We will be making this again. Thank you!
Added a tablespoon of cornstarch with cold water to thicken as mixture was simmering. Used mix frozen berries and orange jus ice instead of water. Was great for Easter brunch!

This was super delicious! I made it with fresh berries and just added a bit more water and it was amazing! My whole family loved it, it was just sweet enough but not too sweet! I highly recommend you to make this!
I had to make it sugar free using monkfruit sugar. It made a good topping
Ends up like a jam consistency, but easy and delicious! Will be making again.
This was delicious! Easy to make, not too sweet. We put it on pancakes, pound cake and ice cream.

Simple and easy. Used a bag of frozen mixed berries. Surprised my gf with some protein pancakes heart shaped with some of this and Greek yogurt and was the perfect combo!

Going to try with stevia instead of sugar next time as I don’t usually eat a lot of sugar.
